CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
27-year-old female here for annual visit. Patient reports she has been doing better overall. She has been struggling with depression, particularly over the past year while working remotely and being confined inside, with off and on struggles with symptoms. She is currently on Prozac 20 mg daily and reports compliance with the medication. She notes the medication has helped her in the past and would like to increase the dose to help get through the current difficult period. Patient also reports chronic back pain that she has been managing. Pain worsens when sitting for long periods at her desk at work but improves with movement and standing. She denies numbness and tingling down her legs or leg pain. She reports some numbing in her legs that feels like it's "falling asleep." She denies leg weakness. Symptoms improve when standing or changing position. She is able to perform activities of daily living, exercise, and go to the store. Pain is bothered by extremes of sitting or standing for too long. Patient had a congenital coronary artery anomaly requiring coronary artery bypass grafting at a young age. She reports her heart has been doing well and her arteries have been looking good.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies numbness and tingling down legs. Denies leg pain or weakness. Reports some numbing sensation in legs. Chronic back pain as noted above.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, chronic back pain, congenital coronary artery anomaly s/p CABG

MEDICATIONS
Prozac 20 mg daily, aspirin

ALLERGIES
Not discussed

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works at desk

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Does not appear in distress. Neck: No thyroid enlargement. Cardiovascular: Three out of six systolic ejection murmur, stable. Pulmonary: Lungs clear. Abdomen: Soft. Musculoskeletal: Pain to palpation of lumbar spine, decreased flexion of back. Extremities: Lower extremity strength good, no edema.

RESULTS
ECG: Basically unchanged from last year. Lumbar spine x-ray: Stable from last year.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Depression: Increase Prozac from 20 mg to 40 mg once daily. Chronic back pain: Refer to physical therapy. Patient declined pain medication at this time, prefers to start with physical therapy. Coronary artery disease s/p CABG: Order echocardiogram. Continue aspirin 81 mg daily.
